claim: An aggregator estimate puts the YouTube channel pyramid at roughly 115 million channels globally, about 10 million with 1,000+ subscribers, 687,909 with 100,000+, 74,969 with 1M+ and 17 with 100M+, implying that under 9% of channels ever reach the subscriber floor for monetization.
stance_target: The overwhelming majority of channels never reach the threshold at which any monetization is possible
scope_conditions: Photutorial, updated June 2026, author Matic Broz; an affiliate-monetized aggregator that compiles Social Blade, vidIQ, Sprout Social, DemandSage, Epidemic Sound and Forbes rather than collecting data; the page itself concedes YouTube publishes no channel census; the six-figure precision of 687,909 and 74,969 against a rounded 'about 115 million' denominator is false precision, and no country breakdown exists
quoted_support: Channel-count estimates vary because many channels are inactive, empty, auto-generated, brand-owned, or used only for subscriptions/comments.

claim: Forbes' 2025 Top Creators ranking put MrBeast at an estimated $85 million, Dhar Mann at $56 million and Jake Paul at $50 million, figures orders of magnitude above any plausible median and drawn from diversified businesses rather than platform ad revenue.
stance_target: Mean creator income is dominated by an extreme right tail and is not a meaningful measure of typical earnings
scope_conditions: Forbes estimates as relayed by Photutorial, an aggregator, not read from the Forbes original; 2025; US creators; the aggregator explicitly notes these totals combine AdSense, sponsorships, consumer products, licensing, subscriptions, live events and platform deals
quoted_support: Forbes ranked him No. 1 on its 2025 Top Creators list with estimated earnings of $85 million and 634 million followers across platforms.
